question: does per-fold peak skew explain why §CI's refit uplift factor varies, as §DA.4 claimed on a single observation?

DA4_claim_under_test.as_written: max/mean depends on per-fold peak skew (F1 1.440, F2 1.954), and that is why F1's uplift is 1.000 and F2's is 2.362
DA4_claim_under_test.why_one_is_not_enough: M2 F1's uplift is 1.000 by construction because §CI fitted k_final on that fold, so it carries no independent information; M2 F2 was the only real point

k_final_reproduction.conclusion: k_final was fitted on M2 F1, so that fold's mean-basis uplift is 1.000 by construction and is circular, not evidence

M1_own_k_final.note: k is family-specific (§CK.4/D14), so M1's folds must be evaluated against M1's own k, not M2's

panels_shared_between_M1_and_M2.note: M2 has no report.json (four folds incomplete), so its fold->dataset map comes from the frozen bundle model cards plus search-record bindings; only folds present in both carriers are compared

M1_three_independent.reading: within M1 alone the rank correlation is NEGATIVE: the fold with the highest skew (F4, 1.857) has the LOWEST mean-basis uplift (1.364). A driver would not reverse sign on the carrier where it can be tested with three points.

correlations.note: with n=3 and n=4 these correlations carry almost no power and are reported as descriptive, not inferential; the point is the SIGN DISAGREEMENT between the pooled and within-M1 views, which is what makes 'skew drives the uplift' untenable as a stated mechanism

THE_REFUTATION.test: if skew drove the uplift, folds with nearly equal skew must have nearly equal uplift
THE_REFUTATION.verdict: REFUTED as a general driver: M1 F2/F3/F4 have skews within 1.8% of each other (1.329-1.353) yet mean-basis uplifts differing by 1.33x (1.364-1.811). Skew therefore does not explain the spread among those three folds. It remains consistent with the single high-skew case (M2 F2, skew 1.748, uplift 2.362), but one consistent case is not a relation.

WHAT_SURVIVES.mean_vs_max_mismatch_is_real: switching the basis cuts the uplift's coefficient of variation from 0.2349 to 0.1303, about half, and cuts the spread from 1.7313x to 1.3399x
WHAT_SURVIVES.residual_not_explained: max-basis uplifts are still 1.0084-1.3512, not 1.0, so a residual factor remains and is NOT identified with four folds
candidates_not_tested: worker contention differing between a 3-task parallel refit and a 72-task grid
fixed measurement error of short spans: M1's refit spans are 0.58-1.92 h and the checkpoint-mtime window omits startup and teardown, which §CK.4 already flagged as dominating short spans

synthetic_control_v.design: four synthetic refit stages whose wall-clock is EXACTLY k_true x epr_max x rows, with peaks drawn to give varied skew
synthetic_control_v.reading: if the mean/max mismatch were the WHOLE story, the real data's max-basis uplifts would all be 1.0 as they are here; they are 1.008-1.351 instead, so the residual is a property of the data and not an artefact of this estimator
